evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Inspectors found staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community" By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 33 minutes ago Young people at a council-owned children's home were found to have tattooed themselves and others with illegally bought kit, a government watchdog found. An Ofsted inspector discovered staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community". The home was rated 'inadequate' by Ofsted and handed three compliance notices to improve children's safety and welfare. A Salford City Council spokesperson said: "We accepted the findings of the inspection in full and have already taken swift action to address the issues raised, resulting in recent positive feedback from Ofsted." "Children now have multiple permanent tattoos which may impact their future choices and opportunities," the inspector wrote in their report. "And children did not receive appropriate medical support and remained exposed to potential health risks." The report also found that staff applied consequences "punitively", with children's bus fares regularly withheld, including for travel to family contact. Inspectors described the practice as "excessive and unreasonable" and noted the type of punishment "does not promote children's welfare or relationships with their families". evidence_packet.evidence_text: Car and moped seized after drivers ignore Heywood lollipop man - BBC News Image caption, Barry Jones was standing in the road when both drivers failed to stop By George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 2 hours ago Police have seized a car and a moped after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man on two separate occasions, forcing him to leap out of the way. Barry Jones was standing in Bury Old Road in Heywood, Greater Manchester, when the incidents happened on 13 and 14 October, Rochdale Borough Council said. Nobody was injured in either incident. The council said 137 incidents of drivers failing to stop for school crossing patrols had been reported across authority area over the past five years. The council said body-worn cameras were now being used in areas where drivers frequently failed to stop to deter dangerous driving and support possible prosecutions. Paul Clarke, a team leader for traffic police community support officers at GMP, said officers had considered the evidence and circumstances before deciding to seize the vehicles. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ex-Britain First leader arrested in HMO attacks investigation - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Ashlea Simon said she was arrested after her social media posts visiting HMOs in Salford By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 27 October 2026 The former co-leader of the far-right Britain First party has said she was arrested as part of an investigation into attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs). In a post on X, Ashlea Simon said she had been held at Manchester Airport after "returning from a family holiday". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a 37-year-old woman had been arrested on suspicion of "conspiracy to cause criminal damage", following a spate of incidents in which HMOs were vandalised across the Greater Manchester region. Simon, who said in her post that she "hasn't committed a crime in her life", was approached for comment by the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS). In the post, Simon said she believed the arrest was linked to a series of videos she has made since July. In them, she claimed to identify several HMOs in her hometown of Walkden, Salford. In a previous video shared by Simon in recent days, she said police had "raided" her home while she was on holiday and she was aware of an "arrest warrant". Simon left Britain First two years ago, and is now the leader of a "pro-English" activism group. The news of her arrest came amid a major investigation into a number of vandalism attacks across Salford, Tameside, and Stockport. Police are investigating about 50 incidents in which HMOs and family homes have been vandalised and cars targeted. In one incident, a pig's head was left outside a home. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five injured in M6 crash as motorway remains partially closed - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, The collision on the northbound M6 in Cheshire caused lengthy delays By Angela Ferguson North West Published 27 October 2026 Five people have been injured in a crash involving a van and a car that resulted in the closure of a motorway in both directions, causing severe delays. Cheshire Police said the collision happened at about 03:30 GMT on the northbound M6 at junction 20 near Warrington, where it meets the M56 at Lymm Interchange. A North West Ambulance Service spokesperson said five people had been taken to hospital, two of whom with serious injuries. The traffic monitoring service Inrix said both carriageways had since reopened. Traffic England said vehicles had been diverted off the M6 via the exit and entry slip roads and later reported delays of 90 minutes, with tailbacks stretching eight miles (13km). Inrix said southbound traffic had built up to junction 22 for Newton-le-Willows, while those heading northbound queued back towards junction 18 for Middlewich and Holmes Chapel. evidence_packet.summary: Police have seized a car and a moped after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man on two separate occasions, forcing him to leap out of the way Barry Jones was standing in Bury Old Road in Heywood, Greater Manchester, when the incidents happened on 13 and 14 October, Roc
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police have seized a car and a moped after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man on two separate occasions, forcing him to leap out of the way Barry Jones was standing in Bury Old Road in Heywood, Greater Manchester, when the incidents happened on 13 and 14 October, Rochdale Borough Council said The council said 137 incidents of drivers failing to stop for school crossing patrols had been reported across authority area over the past five years Greater Manchester Police seized the silver Skoda car and moped after gathering evidence, including witness statements The law was changed in June to remove the requirement for police to issue a warning before seizing vehicles under the Police Reform Act 2002 Dylan Williams, cabinet member for highways, thanked police for their "quick and decisive action" and said the council would keep reporting incidents and push for prosecutions where possible

evidence_packet.title: Ex-Britain First leader arrested in HMO attacks investigation
evidence_packet.lead: The former co-leader of the far-right Britain First party has said she was arrested as part of an investigation into attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) In a post on X, Ashlea Simon said she had been held at Manchester Airport after "returning from a family holiday" G
evidence_packet.summary: The former co-leader of the far-right Britain First party has said she was arrested as part of an investigation into attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) In a post on X, Ashlea Simon said she had been held at Manchester Airport after "returning from a family holiday" G
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The former co-leader of the far-right Britain First party has said she was arrested as part of an investigation into attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) In a post on X, Ashlea Simon said she had been held at Manchester Airport after "returning from a family holiday" Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a 37-year-old woman had been arrested on suspicion of "conspiracy to cause criminal damage", following a spate of incidents in which HMOs were vandalised across the Greater Manchester region Simon, who said in her post that she "hasn't committed a crime in her life", was approached for comment by the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) In the post, Simon said she believed the arrest was linked to a series of videos she has made since July In them, she claimed to identify several HMOs in her hometown of Walkden, Salford

title: Simon Richardson 'selfish' for crash but not murderer, jury told

evidence_packet.title: Simon Richardson 'selfish' for crash but not murderer, jury told
evidence_packet.lead: Warning: This article contains distressing content A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Cr
evidence_packet.summary: Warning: This article contains distressing content A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Cr
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of the murder of head teacher Michael Mullins, 56, who was knocked off his bike as he travelled home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester Prosecutors say Richardson knew Mullins was underneath his car shortly after the collision but drove on anyway, which he denies Mullins became entangled in the suspension of Richardson's Volvo XC90 and was dragged for 2.2km (1.4 miles) after the collision in Warburton, near Altrincham, on 20 April The court heard Richardson drove through Give Way markings at a junction in Warburton and collided with Mullins, who went under his vehicle

evidence_packet.summary: Five people have been injured in a crash involving a van and a car that resulted in the closure of a motorway in both directions, causing severe delays Cheshire Police said the collision happened at about 03:30 GMT on the northbound M6 at junction 20 near Warrington, where it mee
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five people have been injured in a crash involving a van and a car that resulted in the closure of a motorway in both directions, causing severe delays Cheshire Police said the collision happened at about 03:30 GMT on the northbound M6 at junction 20 near Warrington, where it meets the M56 at Lymm Interchange A North West Ambulance Service spokesperson said five people had been taken to hospital, two of whom with serious injuries The traffic monitoring service Inrix said both carriageways had since reopened Traffic England said vehicles had been diverted off the M6 via the exit and entry slip roads and later reported delays of 90 minutes, with tailbacks stretching eight miles (13km) Inrix said southbound traffic had built up to junction 22 for Newton-le-Willows, while those heading northbound queued back towards junction 18 for Middlewich and Holmes Chapel

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Greater Manchester Police officer said man who died from horror injuries 'brought it on himself a little bit' While there is no suggestion PC Gary Knight's actions in any way contributed to the man's death, he was given a wri Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 05:55, 28 Oct 2026 Updated 06:44, 28 Oct 2026 A pensioner who suffered a lacerated scalp, fractured ribs and a collapsed lung in a suspected assault - later dying in hospital - 'brought it on himself a little bit', a police PC Gary Knight has been given a written warning following his dealings with the man in June 2024. He was the subject of a Greater Manchester Police misconduct hearing, with papers summarising force bosses' findings published this week The panel was told a report the man had been assaulted was made between 11.10pm and 11.41pm. On arrival, PC Knight was told he had 'fallen backwards and hit his head' The officer contacted GMP control and said: "[The man]'s got a nasty whack to the back of his head and a cut on his cheek that matches up to falling over - believe he has been intoxicated and stumbled over to the wrong address - ambulance on scene." The panel heard it transpired PC Knight had previously encountered the man, in November, 2023, after he appeared 'drunk and having suffered a blackout, cuts and bruising, and having to be helped home by a member of the public'

An operator for the e-scooters has not yet been considered, the town hall said It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford council said has been a major success. evidence_packet.summary: Bee Network Greater Manchester has a brand-new police force as first arrests made at Piccadilly People were pictured arrested at Manchester Piccadilly by the brand-new police team Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06 The rain lashes the platform
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bee Network Greater Manchester has a brand-new police force as first arrests made at Piccadilly People were pictured arrested at Manchester Piccadilly by the brand-new police team Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06 The rain lashes the platform of the Piccadilly tram stop as commuters brave a miserable Monday morning. For two travellers, the misery is compounded as they are carted away in handcuffs by police officers who were diligently patrolling the Metrolink These officers and perhaps arrests will soon be a familiar site for voyaging Mancunians. The uniformed cops are part of the brand-new Transport Police and Crime Command team, also known as TPACC The unit has been created to provide coverage of the roads, Metrolink and bus services across Greater Manchester. It officially launches on Thursday (October 29), but officers from the group were already in operation on Monday (October 26) The team was originally signed off by Andy Burnham during his stint as a mayor. The project has been previously referred to as the GMP’s ‘11th district’, but the unit has had to wait for the greenlight due to a series of elections View 4 Images Officers will tackle crime and anti-social behaviour on the transport network (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

View Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 05:58, 28 Oct 2026 Updated 05:58, 28 Oct 2026 Greater Manchester is on the cusp of getting enormous new power over its future. Mayors including Bev Craig are set to keep a bigger share of business rates, The move was announced by the government earlier this year and is set to be rolled out from spring 2027. Bev Caig said it could mean Greater Manchester is soon able to fund major infrastructure projects such as tram extensions by itself, without going ‘cap in hand’ to Westminster It comes as political leaders across the country will be watching Chancellor John Healey’s first budget on Wednesday (October 28) Mayor of Greater Manchester Ms Craig said: “The previous mayor and combined authority leaders talked about the ability of the tram to go to Stockport , talked about tram-train in the northeast of the region, all of that is work that is underway, but did not have a funding stream “Retained business rates over a long period of time would let me be able to say, 'okay, I've got certainty for the next 20 years against this level of growth. I can therefore borrow to take the tram-train to Heywood '

evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police Greater Manchester Police officer said man who died from horror injuries 'brought it on himself a little bit' While there is no suggestion PC Gary Knight's actions in any way contributed to the man's death, he was given a wri Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Greater Manchester Police officer said man who died from horror injuries 'brought it on himself a little bit' While there is no suggestion PC Gary Knight's actions in any way contributed to the man's death, he was given a wri Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 05:55, 28 Oct 2026 Updated 06:44, 28 Oct 2026 A pensioner who suffered a lacerated scalp, fractured ribs and a collapsed lung in a suspected assault - later dying in hospital - 'brought it on himself a little bit', a police PC Gary Knight has been given a written warning following his dealings with the man in June 2024. He was the subject of a Greater Manchester Police misconduct hearing, with papers summarising force bosses' findings published this week The panel was told a report the man had been assaulted was made between 11.10pm and 11.41pm. On arrival, PC Knight was told he had 'fallen backwards and hit his head' The officer contacted GMP control and said: "[The man]'s got a nasty whack to the back of his head and a cut on his cheek that matches up to falling over - believe he has been intoxicated and stumbled over to the wrong address - ambulance on scene." The panel heard it transpired PC Knight had previously encountered the man, in November, 2023, after he appeared 'drunk and having suffered a blackout, cuts and bruising, and having to be helped home by a member of the public'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rapist arrested at Manchester Airport after arriving back in UK found guilty He had fled the country in 2020 while under investigation Add to preferred sources News Tom Burnett Night Editor 21:31, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 07:03, 28 Oct 2026 View Image Muha A rapist who was arrested at Manchester Airport after fleeing the country more than half a decade ago has been found guilty of a series of sex offences Muhammed Khalid, aged 55 and from Huddersfield, fled the UK in 2020 while under police investigation for a range of offences allegedly committed in the late 90s and early 2000s On April 23 this year, Khalid was arrested at Manchester Airport after returning to Britain Earlier today he was found guilty of eight offences including rape, sexual assault and supplying Class A drugs following a seven-day trial at Leeds Crown Court The jury found him guilty of five counts of rape, and an offence of sexual assault against one survivor, with offending taking place in the Kirklees area and involving two victims

evidence_packet.summary: Wigan 24-hour gym in Standish opened without planning permission approved after owner's emotional plea Wigan's planning committee heard that Trans4orm in Standish is 'making a difference to people’s lives' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris A 24-hour gym which opened ea
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 24-hour gym in Standish opened without planning permission approved after owner's emotional plea Wigan's planning committee heard that Trans4orm in Standish is 'making a difference to people’s lives' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris A 24-hour gym which opened earlier this year without planning permission has been granted approval by councillors Trans4orm, on Bradley Lane, Standish, has operated from the former Douglas Valley Breakers premises within the Bradley Hall Trading Estate, since June 20 this year Wigan council’s planning committee considered a retrospective application for a change of use for the premises into a round-the-clock gym along with an extension of an upper floor and installation of mezzanine level The council received 91 representations of support and 26 objections to the plans. Supporters said the use said it would support health and wellbeing, employment and a growing population in the town Objectors raised concerns about parking, traffic and over-saturation of such gyms

He had limited mobility. A family friend became concerned after being unable to contact him after December 27 last year She did not have a key, but made several attempts to see Mr Crabbe. As her concerns grew, she contacted Greater Manchester Police for help In a report, senior coroner Alison Mutch said: “She was told that as she could not see him within the flat that it was not a police matter. The advice was to call Stockport Homes when they reopened the next day, or it might be worth trying the ambulance service “The following day Stockport Homes were contacted as soon as they reopened. evidence_packet.summary: Manchester E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027 It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:48, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 18 A fleet of electric scooters
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027 It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:48, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 18 A fleet of electric scooters could be zipping around Manchester next year after the city announced it is exploring plans for a new trial The council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027. An operator for the e-scooters has not yet been considered, the town hall said It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford council said has been a major success. A Manchester council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trail has not yet been made They added: “A provisional approval has been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester "Summer 2027 is the latest a trial could start in line DfT requirements for new trials.”

For two travellers, the misery is compounded as they are carted away in handcuffs by police officers who were diligently patrolling the Metrolink These officers and perhaps arrests will soon be a familiar site for voyaging Mancunians. The uniformed cops are part of the brand-new Transport Police and Crime Command team, also known as TPACC The unit has been created to provide coverage of the roads, Metrolink and bus services across Greater Manchester. It officially launches on Thursday (October 29), but officers from the group were already in operation on Monday (October 26) The team was originally signed off by Andy Burnham during his stint as a mayor. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Greater Manchester Police officer said man who died from horror injuries 'brought it on himself a little bit' While there is no suggestion PC Gary Knight's actions in any way contributed to the man's death, he was given a wri Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 05:55, 28 Oct 2026 Updated 06:44, 28 Oct 2026 A pensioner who suffered a lacerated scalp, fractured ribs and a collapsed lung in a suspected assault - later dying in hospital - 'brought it on himself a little bit', a police PC Gary Knight has been given a written warning following his dealings with the man in June 2024. He was the subject of a Greater Manchester Police misconduct hearing, with papers summarising force bosses' findings published this week The panel was told a report the man had been assaulted was made between 11.10pm and 11.41pm. On arrival, PC Knight was told he had 'fallen backwards and hit his head' The officer contacted GMP control and said: "[The man]'s got a nasty whack to the back of his head and a cut on his cheek that matches up to falling over - believe he has been intoxicated and stumbled over to the wrong address - ambulance on scene." The panel heard it transpired PC Knight had previously encountered the man, in November, 2023, after he appeared 'drunk and having suffered a blackout, cuts and bruising, and having to be helped home by a member of the public'

Mayors including Bev Craig are set to keep a bigger share of business rates, The move was announced by the government earlier this year and is set to be rolled out from spring 2027. Bev Caig said it could mean Greater Manchester is soon able to fund major infrastructure projects such as tram extensions by itself, without going ‘cap in hand’ to Westminster It comes as political leaders across the country will be watching Chancellor John Healey’s first budget on Wednesday (October 28) Mayor of Greater Manchester Ms Craig said: “The previous mayor and combined authority leaders talked about the ability of the tram to go to Stockport , talked about tram-train in the northeast of the region, all of that is work that is underway, but did not have a funding stream “Retained business rates over a long period of time would let me be able to say, 'okay, I've got certainty for the next 20 years against this level of growth. I can therefore borrow to take the tram-train to Heywood '

title: E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027

evidence_packet.title: E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027 It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:48, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 18 A fleet of electric scooters
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027 It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:48, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 18 A fleet of electric scooters
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester E-scooters could be coming to Manchester with trial set to launch in 2027 It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:48, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 18 A fleet of electric scooters could be zipping around Manchester next year after the city announced it is exploring plans for a new trial The council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027. An operator for the e-scooters has not yet been considered, the town hall said It comes off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford council said has been a major success. A Manchester council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trail has not yet been made They added: “A provisional approval has been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester "Summer 2027 is the latest a trial could start in line DfT requirements for new trials.”

Shortly before 6am this morning, October 27, officers from team Operation Vulcan carried out a warrant on Buxton Road as part of their work on tac As a result, officers recovered 150 to 200 wraps of crack cocaine and heroin. To his critics, he’s a charismatic flip-flopper relying on small ge Add to preferred sources News Iram Ramzan 16:37, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 16:41, 27 Oct 2026 When Mohammed returned from his Thursday outreach session in Ashton-in-Makerfield, he had a story to tell his colleague Sheilagh Linde. He had met a man called ‘Andy’ “Two weeks later he said, ‘oh we’ve got a new MP’. I said ‘yeah, you met him!’ Sheilagh laughs. “He was surprised.” The new MP, as you may have guessed, was Andy Burnham It is a small anecdote, but one that gets to the heart of Mr Burnham’s political appeal. Here was a man who could spend time talking to somebody doing outreach work with refugees without being recognised as a politician, let alone the man who would soon be prime minister Mr Burnham has spent much of his political career cultivating this familiarity. Unlike some politicians, he seems comfortable without a script. He is the type of person, as several have put it to me, that you might meet in a pub In order to launch a leadership challenge against prime minister Keir Starmer, the mayor of Greater Manchester first had to become an MP. And so Josh Simons stood down in Makerfield, paving the path for Mr Burnham

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Falconer Chester Hall had helped draw up the outline plans for Oakmere Homes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

A serious illness, the loss of a loved one, or something unexpected affecting your ability to work can turn life upside down overnight. Would you know what to do next? This is what I often refer to as a "lifeboat moment" – when normal life stops and you're forced to navigate a completely different reality Planning for a lifeboat moment means having some really difficult conversations. What would happen if you weren't around? If your income stopped tomorrow? If you had to manage the finances on your own? For many, the biggest challenges are surprisingly practical. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of the murder of head teacher Michael Mullins, 56, who was knocked off his bike as he travelled home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester Prosecutors say Richardson knew Mullins was underneath his car shortly after the collision but drove on anyway, which he denies Mullins became entangled in the suspension of Richardson's Volvo XC90 and was dragged for 2.2km (1.4 miles) after the collision in Warburton, near Altrincham, on 20 April The court heard Richardson drove through Give Way markings at a junction in Warburton and collided with Mullins, who went under his vehicle A motorcyclist followed a trail of blood and discovered Mullins alone and barely breathing as he lay on a grass verge in a secluded country lane in Lymm, Cheshire

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Police is taking part in Operation Insight, a national road safety initiative to improve road safety through raising awareness of vulnerable road users and the importance of being fit to drive Roadside vision screenings on motorists of all ages began on Monday and will continue until 8 November Ch Insp Cameron Taylor, Cheshire Police's head of roads and crime, said: "Our message is simple: if you drive, make sure your eyesight is checked regularly and that you wear any corrective lenses you need." A Cheshire Police spokesperson said around 3,000 people across the country were seriously injured each year in crashes involving drivers or riders with uncorrected or defective eyesight In 2025, 18 people lost their lives on UK roads as a result of vision-related factors, they added During roadside screenings, officers will ask drivers to read a vehicle registration plate from the legally required distance of 66ft (20m), under appropriate daylight conditions and while wearing any corrective lenses they normally use for driving

evidence_packet.evidence_text: With Manchester's world-famous Christmas Markets opening in just over a week, the design of this year's iconic limited edition Christmas mugs has been revealed - and fans of Manchester's giant Santa, who returns to Albert Square this festive season for the first time in nearly a The retro-style design shows Manchester's favourite giant Santa surrounded by gift-wrapped presents and fir trees, all set against a night sky as the snow falls gently down on a cityscape of Manchester, with the Town Hall and its unmistakable clock tower to one side Designed by the city council's in-house design studio the mugs are the latest in a series of collectable Christmas mugs designed by them each year for Manchester's world-beating Christmas Markets There are two different souvenir mugs to collect. evidence_packet.title: More than £3m of support secured for Mancunians through game-changing Citizens Advice hospital trial
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Litter and leaves swept up by new investment – Bolton Council Published: Tuesday, 27th Oct 2026 Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping. New road sweepers have been purchased, bigger bins installed at key spots and handy equipment stores provided for volunteer litter pickers. A fleet of road sweepers in various sizes are used by the council to remove leaves and litter, and there have been several recent additions. One large sweeper has been added, making three in total, and these are vital for keeping roads and drains clear of leaves and twigs in autumn, which reduces the risk of flooding as well as keeping streets looking tidy. Six smaller mechanical sweepers are used on pavements, with teams focusing on different areas of Bolton on a rotating schedule. A new electrically powered pavement sweeper has also been brought in that can get into smaller spaces like cycle lanes, helping to keep them clean and safe to use. The sweepers are among the equipment used by Environmental Services teams who spent the summer doing things like cutting grass and spraying weeds, and who have now switched to autumn jobs like gathering leaves. They target routes such as Chorley New Road and Gilnow Road that have lots of trees and remove the leaves and detritus they produce. Bigger roads are also benefiting from new, larger litter bins as part of a major programme of improvements on Bolton’s main transport routes. Almost 50 bins have been replaced with ones that have more than twice the capacity, meaning they are less likely to get full and cause litter to overflow onto the street. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.summary: Five days. Five themes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. Manchester Digital Festival returns from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringing together bus Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

title: Manchester Digital helps shape government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Digital helps shape government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Applications are now open for MentorHER Cohort 4 , Manchester Digital's mentoring programme connecting women at the beginning of their digital and technology careers with experienced professionals across the industry Launched to coincide with Ada Lovelace Day, the fourth cohort of MentorHER will run from January to July 2027, delivered through Manchester Digital's DigitalHER programme in partnership with Autotrader The six-month programme aims to help women build confidence, develop their professional skills and establish valuable connections as they navigate the early stages of their careers in digital and technology Applications are now open for both mentors and mentees, with a deadline of Sunday 8 November 2026 Building a successful career in technology is about more than technical skills. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.summary: Little Wander in association with PBJ Management present Amy Matthews: Definitions of Toast Amy doesn't get angry and she's starting to feel left out, so she's on a quest to feel fury; from what she can discern from the world around her, it appears to be all the rage... literally
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Little Wander in association with PBJ Management present Amy Matthews: Definitions of Toast Amy doesn't get angry and she's starting to feel left out, so she's on a quest to feel fury; from what she can discern from the world around her, it appears to be all the rage... literally Amy is navigating the joy of her first queer relationship whilst dusting herself off from a string of several alcoholic partners. You'd think she'd have plenty to be cross about, and yet, whilst everyone seems to be more furious than ever, she just can't seem to tap into her own This lack of wrath may also have something to do with a processing lag that is becoming increasingly disruptive - and comical - in her life. Her emotions seemed to be delivered by carrier pigeon, if they arrive at all This is a show about being Best Supporting Actor in one's own life, queer joy, and how a potion from 2002 cursed the world "Drily funny and giddily quirky." (The Scotsman)

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. We don’t want to predict on that, but he’s not ready for the next games.” Alonso clarified that João Pedro would “probably” be out until after next month’s international break, meaning he will not be available for Brazil after missing the last camp with a knee issue. evidence_packet.evidence_text: For the second year running, our friends from the AI Café are back to make sure you leave the festival with more questions than you arrived with. Their plan is simple: to excite you, astound you and make you take stock of just how quickly this field is moving Expect a relaxed, afternoon of conversations about artificial intelligence, its ethics, the future of work and what might come next, alongside talks from people working at the cutting edge of AI If you're a technologist, business leader, students or just curious about AI, this is for you. No expert knowledge required 📅 Date: Friday 12th February 2027 🕒 Time: 15:30-17:00 📍 Location: TBC 🎟️ Tickets: £10 (Early Bird) £15 (Standard) Free (Manchester Digital Members) Manchester Digital members - check your recent emails or speak to your membership manager for your free discount code This event is part of the Manchester Digital Festival 2027, a week long event bringing together the businesses, talent and leadership powering Greater Manchester's tech sector. Find out more about the festival and other ways to get involved via the link below

They'll be diving into the UK Budget and giving a 2027 Economic and Currency Market Outlook. Our Partner experts will be on Monex is a global financial services group with more than 40 years of experience helping businesses navigate global markets through foreign exchange expertise, market insights, and risk management solutions. Through its top-ranked research team, Monex is regularly recognised amon Representing Monex at this year's Forum will be Dr. Nick Rees , Head of Macro Research at Monex, alongside Katie Bragol i, Head of Corporate Sales, and Alex Kiddell, Executive from Monex UK During the event, Nick will explore the key geopolitical and macroeconomic themes shaping the global business environment as we look towards 2027. Drawing on insights from Monex's research team, he will discuss potential market implications arising from fiscal policy developments
